topics.name: Theory of Consumer Behaviour
topics.note: Fast session 2026-10-07 (quiz not graded); being re-taught in classroom mode

subtopics.name: Preferences: completeness, transitivity, monotonicity, convexity, continuity; lexicographic preferences; ordinal utility and monotonic transformations
Cardinal utility (Marshall): diminishing marginal utility, equi-marginal principle, water-diamond paradox
Indifference curves, budget line, consumer equilibrium (MRS = price ratio); perfect substitutes and perfect complements; corner solutions; utility maximisation numericals
Income effect: income-consumption curve (ICC), Engel curve, normal / inferior / luxury goods, Engel's law
Price effect: substitution and income effects (Hicks and Slutsky versions), Giffen goods, why demand slopes down; income and substitution effects of a tax
Revealed preference (Samuelson): weak and strong axioms; why it cannot explain the Giffen case
Demand: inverse demand function, complements/substitutes, exceptions to the law of demand (Veblen, snob, bandwagon)

Elasticities: price (point, arc, on linear and parallel demand curves, constant-elasticity form), income, cross; relation of MR, AR and elasticity; sum of elasticities = 0 (homogeneity); elasticity and total revenue; supply elasticity of a line through the origin
Consumer surplus (Marshall): definition, calculation from a demand function by integration
Duality: indirect utility function, expenditure function, Marshallian vs Hicksian demand, Roy's identity, Shephard's lemma, Slutsky equation; Gorman form (aggregation)
History: chronology of consumer theories (Marshall 1890 → Hicks-Allen 1934 → Samuelson 1938 → Stone's linear expenditure system 1954); who did what
Short-run production: TP, AP, MP; law of variable proportions and its three stages
Isoquants, MRTS, ridge lines and the economic region; least-cost combination (MRTS = w/r); second-order conditions; expansion path
Returns to scale; homogeneous and homothetic functions; Euler's theorem; properties of a function homogeneous of degree 1 (MPs homogeneous of degree 0)
Cobb-Douglas (output elasticities, MPs, RTS = α+β, σ = 1), CES (σ = 1/(1+ρ)), Leontief (σ = 0); elasticity of substitution
Short-run cost curves: TFC, TVC, AFC, AVC, AC, MC; relations (MC cuts AVC and AC at minima; AFC falls continuously); MC from TC; minimum AC from a cost function
Long-run costs: LAC as envelope, economies and diseconomies of scale, learning curve, optimum firm

Cost function and duality: properties of the cost function (homogeneous of degree 1 in input prices, concave), Shephard's lemma (conditional factor demands), cost function of perfect-substitute technology, Hotelling's lemma

topics.name: Decision making under uncertainty; attitude towards risk

subtopics.name: Expected value vs expected utility; von Neumann-Morgenstern utility; choosing with an equal expected income
Risk aversion, neutrality, loving (concave/linear/convex utility; indifference-curve view); certainty equivalent; risk premium
Reducing risk: diversification, insurance, value of information; mean-standard-deviation choice
Normal-form games; strictly and weakly dominant/dominated strategies; iterated elimination
Nash equilibrium: pure, multiple equilibria (battle of the sexes, stag hunt), no pure equilibrium (matching pennies), mixed strategies
Zero-sum games: saddle point, value of the game, maximin/minimax (von Neumann-Morgenstern)
Prisoners' dilemma and repeated games: tit-for-tat (Axelrod), grim trigger
Sequential games: backward induction, subgame-perfect equilibrium; Cournot and Stackelberg as Nash equilibria

topics.name: Market structures: competitive and non-competitive equilibria and their efficiency

subtopics.name: Perfect competition: short- and long-run equilibrium, normal profit, shutdown, efficiency (P = MC = min LAC)
Market equilibrium and its stability: Walrasian and Marshallian stability, cobweb model (convergent, explosive, oscillating)
Welfare in a market: consumer and producer surplus, deadweight loss, price floors, monopoly vs competition comparison
Monopoly: MR = MC, MR-AR-elasticity relation, Lerner index, no supply curve, deadweight loss; profit-maximisation numericals; taxing a monopolist (lump-sum vs per-unit)
Price discrimination: degrees, conditions, the elasticity rule (higher price where demand is less elastic)
Natural monopoly and regulation; public utility pricing; socially optimal price (P = MC)
Monopolistic competition (Chamberlin): product differentiation, excess capacity, advertising/selling costs, Dorfman-Steiner advertising rule
Oligopoly: Cournot, Bertrand, Stackelberg, kinked demand (Sweezy), cartels, price leadership, limit pricing (Bain), full-cost pricing (Hall and Hitch)
Comparing market structures (matching features)
Marginal productivity theory: VMP, MRP, derived demand for labour; competitive vs monopoly product market (VMP > MRP); shifts in labour demand
Product exhaustion (Euler; Clark-Wicksteed); factor shares and the elasticity of substitution
Wages: minimum wage effects (competitive and monopsony), labour-demand elasticity, efficiency wage
Rent: Ricardian rent, quasi-rent (Marshall), modern theory (Joan Robinson), transfer earnings
Interest: time-preference theory (Böhm-Bawerk, Fisher), loanable funds, liquidity preference
Profit: Knight (uncertainty), Schumpeter (innovation), Clark (dynamic), Kalecki (degree of monopoly)
Partial vs general equilibrium; Walrasian system; Walras' law; excess demand functions (homogeneous of degree zero in prices)
Existence, uniqueness, stability; Arrow-Debreu model (goods dated and located; contingent commodities)
Edgeworth box (exchange and production), contract curve, core; production possibility frontier and MRT (MCx/MCy); straight-line PPF

topics.name: Efficiency criteria: Pareto optimality, Kaldor-Hicks, wealth maximisation

subtopics.name: Pareto optimality: definition; three marginal conditions (exchange MRS, production MRTS, product-mix MRS = MRT); technical efficiency
Compensation criteria: Kaldor, Hicks, Scitovsky (double test, reversal paradox), Little

topics.name: Welfare Economics: fundamental theorems, social welfare function

subtopics.name: First and second fundamental theorems and their conditions
Social welfare functions: Bergson-Samuelson, utilitarian (Bentham), Rawlsian (maximin); social indifference curves; utility possibility frontier

topics.name: Asymmetric information: adverse selection and moral hazard

subtopics.name: Adverse selection: Akerlof's market for lemons (Nobel 2001), insurance and credit markets
Signalling (Spence) and screening
Moral hazard (hidden action after the contract), principal-agent; farm-loan waivers as moral hazard

topics.name: Determination of output and employment: Classical and Keynesian approach
Rational Expectations Hypothesis and its critique
Instruments and working of monetary policy
International trade: basic concepts and analytical tools
Balance of Payments: composition, equilibrium, disequilibrium, adjustment mechanisms
Gains from trade, terms of trade, trade multiplier
GATT, WTO and regional trade blocks; trade policy issues
Market failure and remedies: asymmetric information, public goods, externality
Regulation of markets: collusion and consumers' welfare
Public revenue: tax and non-tax, direct and indirect, progressive and non-progressive, incidence and effects of taxation
Concepts and measures: fertility, morbidity, mortality
Theories of development: Smith, Ricardo, Marx, Schumpeter, Rostow, balanced and unbalanced growth, Big Push
Growth models: Harrod-Domar, Solow, Robinson, Kaldor
Technical progress: disembodied and embodied; endogenous growth
Indicators of development: PQLI, HDI, SDGs
Poverty and inequality: concepts and measurement
Social sector development: health, education, gender
Sets, functions and continuity, sequence, series
Static optimisation problems and their applications
Difference and differential equations with applications
Probability theory: concepts, distributions, moments, Central Limit Theorem
Descriptive statistics: central tendency, dispersion, correlation, index numbers
Linear regression models and their properties: BLUE
Simultaneous equation models: recursive and non-recursive
Economic growth in India: pattern and structure
Agriculture: growth pattern, challenges, policy responses
Industry: growth pattern, challenges, policy responses
Services: growth pattern, challenges, policy responses
Rural development: issues, challenges, policy responses
Urban development: issues, challenges, policy responses
Foreign trade: structure and direction, BOP, foreign capital flows, trade policies
Infrastructure development: physical and social; public-private partnerships
Reforms in land, labour and capital markets
Centre-State financial relations, Finance Commissions, FRBM
Teaching: concept, objectives, levels (memory, understanding, reflective), characteristics
Learner's characteristics (adolescent and adult learners), individual differences
Factors affecting teaching (teacher, learner, support material, facilities, environment, institution)
Methods of teaching: teacher- vs learner-centred, offline vs online (SWAYAM, SWAYAM Prabha, MOOCs)
Teaching support system: traditional, modern, ICT-based
Evaluation systems: elements, types, CBCS, computer-based testing, innovations
Research: meaning, types, characteristics; positivism and post-positivism
Methods of research: experimental, descriptive, historical, qualitative, quantitative
Thesis and article writing: format and referencing styles
Sources, acquisition and classification of data
Graphical representation and mapping of data
Number series, letter series, codes and relationships
Mathematical aptitude: fractions, time and distance, ratio, proportion, percentage, profit and loss, interest and discounting, averages
Structure of arguments: forms, categorical propositions, mood and figure, fallacies, uses of language, connotation/denotation, square of opposition
Venn diagrams for validity of arguments
Indian logic: means of knowledge; Pramanas
Anumana (inference): structure and kinds, Vyapti, Hetvabhasas
Effective communication: verbal, non-verbal, inter-cultural, group, classroom
Internet, intranet, e-mail, audio and video conferencing
Development and environment: MDGs and SDGs
Human-environment interaction: anthropogenic activities and impacts
Environmental issues: pollution types, waste, climate change
Impacts of pollutants on human health
EPA 1986, NAPCC, international agreements (Montreal, Rio, CBD, Kyoto, Paris, ISA)
Evolution of higher learning and research after Independence
Reading a passage and answering questions
